thread:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — saw a burst where primary model (redwood/gptx-8k) hit soft-saturation and requests started queueing for ~400ms. Suggest we enable an automatic autoswap to a compatible lower-capacity variant rather than queuing.
Trevor Kim: +1. Can we make that tier-aware? gold customers should never be autoswapped unless latency SLO is about to break.
Linh Nguyen: Agreed on tier-awareness. Also need to track quality regression when swapping -> includes per-customer prompt set evals.
Jorge Alvarez: Quick question: how do we define "saturated"? queue length? CPU/GPU util? pending tokens?
Maya Patel: Good point. Proposal: saturation = queued_requests > q_threshold OR (avg_gpu_util > 92% for 30s) OR tail_latency P95 > 1.2x SLO. Keep it configurable by policy.
Elaine Brooks: From cost POV, autoswapping to a quantized variant can lower token cost. But we should surface estimated cost delta in Console before swap and in telemetry after.
Trevor Kim: UX: Console toggle per-route: "Enable autoswap when saturated" with a dropdown: [Prefer lower-cost variant, Prefer latency, Strict quality]. Default: Prefer latency for enterprise, Prefer cost for self-serve.
Linh Nguyen: Telemetry events we need: variant_autoswap_attempt, variant_autoswap_success, variant_autoswap_rollback, autoswap_trigger_reason. Include fields: customer_tier, route, p95_before, p95_after, cost_delta_est, model_from, model_to, swap_time_ms.
Maya Patel: Example of telemetry schema (rough):
```json
{
  "event":"variant_autoswap_success",
  "customer_tier":"gold",
  "route":"/v1/chat/generate",
  "model_from":"redwood/gptx-8k",
  "model_to":"redwood/gptx-8k-quantized-q2",
  "p95_before_ms":"520",
  "p95_after_ms":"240",
  "cost_delta_pct":"-18",
  "reason":"gpu_util_95pct",
  "timestamp":"2028-06-04T12:34:56Z"
}
```
Jorge Alvarez: For automatic rollback rules: if quality metrics (eval score or error rate) degrade > delta_threshold within 10m -> rollback and mark route as "sensitive" to autoswaps for 1h.
Elaine Brooks: We should also record token/accounting rules: swapped requests must be billed per the model actually used. Console should show a breakdown so customers understand cost changes.
Trevor Kim: Implementation detail: routing layer needs a quick path to check variant compatibility (same tokenizer, same API surface). If not compatible -> don't autoswap, instead fallback to queuing or regional reroute.
Linh Nguyen: Suggest a small API flag clients can set: `fallback_policy=prefer_variant_swap|no_swap|regional_reroute`. Default is server-side policy. That lets power users opt out.
Maya Patel: Example config we could expose in Console and API:
```yaml
route_policy:
  autoswap:
    enabled: true
    sensitivity: medium   # low/medium/high
    prefer: latency
    quality_guard:
      enabled: true
      score_threshold: 0.92
    triggers:
      queued_requests: 20
      gpu_util_pct: 92
      tail_latency_mult: 1.2
```
Jorge Alvarez: How about canary behavior for autoswap? e.g., route 5% of incoming traffic to variant_first before full swap. Prevents big regressions.
Maya Patel: Yes — 3-stage: probe (5%), ramp (50%), full (100%). Probe window 30s, ramp 5m. Abort on quality or latency regressions.
Elaine Brooks: Ops question: need metrics in Console for "autoswap churn" — count of swaps per route/day, % of swaps auto-rolled-back, avg latency delta — for SLA reporting.
Trevor Kim: Dev API change: routing decision should be atomic and idempotent. Also add a dry-run mode so console can simulate swap and show p95 estimates without executing.
Linh Nguyen: For rollout, add a feature flag gated behind runtime config so we can flip it per-cluster. Ops-bot can announce when toggle flips.
ops-bot: DeployBot: feature-toggle autoswap.v1 enabled in cluster eu-west-1 by maya.p (reason: trial).
Jorge Alvarez: Edge case: model variants with slight behavior changes (different tokenizer or different end-of-stream handling). Need a compatibility registry; don't autoswap if compatibility=false.
Maya Patel: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to prototype autoswap decision RFC (Trevor/Linh) 2) metrics + telemetry schema (Jorge/ Elaine) 3) Console UX mock for toggles + dry-run (Maya) 4) policy defaults per tier + API flag (Trevor).
Trevor Kim: I'll grab RFC this week, will post link when done. @Linh can you draft the compatibility registry fields?
Linh Nguyen: On it. I'll include tokenizer hash, sample_inference_tests, and required API surface.
Elaine Brooks: I'll draft the Console mock and include the cost delta visualization.
Maya Patel: Thanks all. If anyone finds urgent saturation events, ping me in #oncall. For tracking: creating a short ticket in eng-platform board.
ops-bot: Ticket created: ENGPLAT-4873 "Autoswap policy prototype" assigned to Trevor Kim
Trevor Kim: Thanks — will update with RFC link and timeline by EOD Friday.
